speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a skin lesion on your chest; can you tell me how long you've had it and if it has changed in size, shape, or color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Basal Cell Carcinoma. A 63-year-old male with a two-month history of an increasing chest lesion, lacking pain or pruritus, and a significant history of type 2 diabetes and hypercholesterolemia presents with clinical features consistent with non-melanoma skin cancer. Requesting a biopsy and dermatologic imaging.
